answer: We formulate a dynamic opportunity-cost bond with staking collateral $C$ and zero-knowledge verifiable delays to anchor the consensus wharf against a tide of identity multiplication. If validators wander from protocol trajectories, subgame-perfect slashing penalties trigger automatically. Consequently, for any adversary replicating identities, the expected utility of attack is strictly negative ($U < 0$), proving that honest participation constitutes the unique, robust Nash equilibrium under all conditions.
